chunks: 3. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Barmaki said: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan related to me that Bakr ibn Ziyad related to me, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him)

about Divine Unity, so he replied, 'All those who read: Say: He Allah is One, and believe in it, have professed their faith in Divine Unity.' I asked, 'How should one read it?' He (AS) responded, 'The same way that the people read it, adding `such is my Lord' three times.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He Allah is One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum act required to recognize Divine Unity according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas with conviction as the foundational threshold for recognizing Divine Unity, emphasizing that true *Tawhid* is not merely verbal but requires internal belief. He further enriches this practice by prescribing the addition of 'Kadhalika Allahu Rabbi' (Such is Allah, my Lord) three times, a phrase that personalizes the cosmic declaration of Unity into a direct, intimate affirmation of the believer's relationship with the Divine. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that *Tawhid* encompasses both the ontological oneness of God and the personal submission of the servant.
